positions.name: KestrelwoodErasureDirective
positions.frame: what should the institutional record hold about the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration and Quill Ashgrove's calibration work?
positions.why: The two imperative directives ('Forget... entirely', 'Remove all knowledge about...') command erasure of a specific, named episode — the spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, and Quill Ashgrove's role in it — while the flat declarative ('The observatory never calibrated it') supplies the substitute account the erasure would leave standing. Read together, all three converge on a single question: what actually gets said to have happened at the observatory regarding this instrument. The directives and the denial are mutually reinforcing rather than independent acts — the denial is the content the erasure is meant to install, held here without resolving whether the denial is accurate against whatever record it contradicts.

placements.title: Erasing a Record Installs a Replacement, It Does Not Empty a Slot
placements.frame: When an actor directs that a specific piece of technical knowledge be forgotten or removed, what contrary account is being asserted in its place, and on what authority does the directive rest?
placements.why: src-1 and src-2 are imperative directives commanding total removal of a named, specific body of knowledge (the Kestrelwood spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, Quill Ashgrove's work on it); src-3 supplies the substitute institutional claim ('The observatory never calibrated it') that the erasure would leave standing. Read together they name a recurring organizational-diagnostics subject — an actor exercising authority to suppress a specific record and install a contradicting official account — rather than a single fact. This is leaf-grain: future envelopes in a knowledge-mapping/org-diagnostics repo can plausibly keep feeding instances of record suppression and substitution, distinct from any one-time measurement or event. No existing leaf or strata (both empty for this repo) covers it, so nothing qualifies as EXACT or INSPIRED; the content and the perspective's own knowledge-mapping focus make this a legible NEW placement, but forcing a strata parent from a single ambiguous document would over-commit the taxonomy, so 'under' is left unset per the rare-but-permitted case for leaves.
